ratings.concept: Secondary growth in a woody dicot stem: the outer-to-inner order phellem → secondary cortex → secondary phloem → wood (secondary xylem)
ratings.strategy_evidence: Phellem is the outermost product of the cork cambium, so the order must open with (d); that one fact strikes options 2 and 3, which open with (c) Secondary phloem and (a) Secondary cortex.

traps.label: sequence_endpoint_or_adjacency
traps.route: keeps both endpoints of the key — (d) Phellem outermost and (b) Wood innermost — and interchanges the single interior adjacency, placing (c) Secondary phloem outside (a) Secondary cortex

ratings.reason: This question requires placing four secondary tissues on the radial axis of a woody dicot stem, demonstrated by the stem's instruction to give the order "with reference to their arrangement from outer side to inner side in a woody dicot stem" over the printed items "(a) Secondary cortex", "(b) Wood", "(c) Secondary phloem", "(d) Phellem".
ratings.note: has_figure is true (figures_agent/2015_A/q118.png) but the stem and the four lettered items are complete and self-contained, so the figure is decorative for this printing and the item is not treated as source_incomplete. Options 2 and 3 carry no nameable route: neither is the reverse of the key (that would be (b),(c),(a),(d)) nor the printed list order (a),(b),(c),(d), so per rulebook rule 4 no trap is written for them.

group_note: Single-member packet. It was grouped on structure=list, and the printed shape is in fact an ordering item — a lettered list of four tissues with an order as the answer — so on E1 it belongs with arrange_in_order rather than with list_of_statements; it was judged against the other ordering item in this run (2015_A#q077, packet v2__biology__statements.part1) and carries the same labels as that one: application (the retirement of sequence_based sends ordering to application), single_step (one radial/temporal axis is laid down, not four independent checks), elimination where one securely-known endpoint strikes options, and sequence_endpoint_or_adjacency for the distractor that keeps the endpoints and swaps one interior adjacency.
